domain_description: The classroom formative cycle — setting clear targets, eliciting evidence of learning, diagnosing gaps, and closing them with usable feedback. All interventions cross-referenced to peer-reviewed meta-analyses where one exists, and to the EEF Toolkit where a matching strand exists.

skills.description: Unpack a competency or standard into the underlying knowledge, skills, and observable success criteria students need to demonstrate.
skills.implementation_cost_rationale: Unpacking standards into success criteria is teacher prep work that can be done once per unit; no new materials, no training beyond awareness, no structural change.

skills.description: Author student-friendly learning targets that tie each target to its broader purpose — what students will be able to do, and why it matters.
skills.implementation_cost_rationale: Authoring learning targets is teacher prep work done once per lesson or unit; no materials, no training beyond awareness of structure.

skills.description: Design a single multiple-choice question, placed at a hinge point in a lesson, whose distractors diagnose specific misconceptions and tell you whether to move on, pause, or reteach.
skills.implementation_cost_rationale: Hinge questions take only 1-2 minutes per lesson to deploy, but writing good ones takes real pedagogical content knowledge — distractors must be anchored in actual misconceptions, not generic plausibility, or the question stops diagnosing anything.

skills.description: Design a structured protocol of formative checks across a lesson — cold call, mini-whiteboards, exit tickets, ABCD cards, hand signals — so every student's understanding is sampled before the lesson ends.
skills.implementation_cost_rationale: Protocol design happens once per unit; the techniques themselves (cold call, mini-whiteboards, exit tickets) need no materials beyond what teachers already have and no training beyond awareness of the technique set.
